title: Auxiliary Power Unit Start and Shutdown — Crew Procedure

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Crew procedure for starting and shutting down the auxiliary power unit, including the cooling period before shutdown and the actions on a failure to start.

sections.purpose: Gives the flight crew the procedure to start and shut down the auxiliary power unit, and the actions to take if it does not respond to a start request.
sections.description: The auxiliary power unit supplies electrical power and air on the ground and, within the flight envelope, in the air. The crew request a start from the overhead panel and the start sequence runs automatically; the crew see the state on the auxiliary power page and no further action is needed until the unit is available. Shutdown is commanded from the same panel, and the unit runs on for a cooling period before it stops. The cooling period is not optional and the crew must not remove electrical power from the aircraft during it, because the run-on is what protects the unit from a heat soak after a period of bleed extraction. If the unit does not respond to a start request at all, with no rotation and no state shown on the page, the crew should not repeat the request more than the number of times given in the operations manual: repeated requests on a unit that is not responding do not help and can complicate the maintenance investigation.
sections.crew_procedure: Request the start from the overhead panel and confirm the state on the auxiliary power page. Wait for the available indication before selecting any load. To shut down, command the shutdown and allow the cooling run-on to complete before removing electrical power. If the unit does not respond to a start request, wait the interval given in the operations manual and request once more. If there is still no response, do not request again; record the occurrence in the technical log with the time and whether any tail cone work had been carried out.

type_data.crew_action: Allow the cooling run-on to complete before removing electrical power; do not repeat a start request more than once.
